{"type": "assistant", "timestamp": "2026-10-23T13:37:16.346Z", "parent_tool_use_id": null, "uuid": "43e5e7df-299b-4fbd-a955-4047818264c7", "session_id": "90f1364c-d20b-4809-9a50-8356132da019", "message": {"model": "claude-sonnet-5-5", "id": "msg_011CgKFzKvfVtDN3PyWiC34n", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_011QUQKtmTN8Qrbzhijcn5Eu", "name": "Bash", "input": {"command": "cd /app/.spektacular/work/20260101000000-user-auth\ncat > architecture.md <<'EOF'\nThe chosen design is a self-contained `auth` package in the `app` repo that owns token issuance, validation and revocation, fronted by an HTTP middleware and three endpoints (`/auth/login`, `/auth/refresh`, `/auth/revoke`). Access tokens are RS256-signed JWTs carrying only user ID and role, expiring after 15 minutes; they are never stored server-side. Public/private keys come from environment config so any instance can verify tokens independently, which delivers cross-instance validation with no shared session state.\n\nRefresh tokens are opaque random values with a 7-day lifetime, stored only as hashes in a `refresh_tokens` PostgreSQL table and rotated on use. Revocation uses a Redis deny list keyed by token ID (`jti`) with a TTL equal to the token's remaining lifetime, so entries age out automatically. The middleware verifies signature and expiry, checks the deny list, and attaches the verified identity to the request context; all failures return a uniform 401 that does not reveal whether a token was malformed or expired. Every auth decision emits an `AUTH_AUDIT_V2` record (see Conventions) without token material. Migration keeps existing endpoints working by running the new middleware alongside session auth behind a switch, then cutting over.\n\nOptions weighed: (A) this stateless JWT + Redis deny list design (Medium effort; meets the 5ms p99 target and spec approach); (B) JWT with a PostgreSQL deny list (Low-Medium effort, but a DB hit per request threatens latency); (C) opaque tokens with introspection (High effort, requires server-side access token storage, forbidden by spec). A wins. Rejected options and citations: see research.md#alternatives-considered-and-rejected.\nEOF\ncat > conventions.md <<'EOF'\n- **Authentication events must emit an AUTH_AUDIT_V2 record** \u2014 login, refresh, revoke and rejected tokens are all auth decisions this feature introduces; records carry user ID, outcome and request ID and never the token.\nEOF\ncat >> assumptions.md <<'EOF'\n\n### Chosen direction: JWT + Redis deny list (architecture)\n- **Decision**: Stateless RS256 JWT access tokens, hashed rotating refresh tokens in PostgreSQL, Redis deny list keyed by jti with TTL.\n- **Rationale**: Matches spec Technical Approach and constraints; lowest per-request latency.\n- **Rejected**: PostgreSQL deny list (latency); opaque tokens with introspection (server-side access token storage forbidden).\n\n### Conventions selection (architecture)\n- **Decision**: Apply only the AUTH_AUDIT_V2 convention (the sole one loaded).\n- **Rationale**: Directly governs every endpoint and the middleware.\n- **Rejected**: Dropping it as optional \u2014 it is a definition-of-done requirement.\n\n### Migration via parallel run (architecture)\n- **Decision**: Run JWT middleware alongside session auth behind a config switch, then cut over.\n- **Rationale**: Satisfies zero-downtime and no-breaking-endpoints constraints.\n- **Rejected**: Big-bang cutover (downtime risk).\nEOF\ncd /app; echo \"- Architecture: JWT+Redis deny list, parallel-run migration.\" >> .spektacular/working-context.md\nspektacular plan goto --data '{\"step\":\"components\",\"name\":\"20260101000000-user-auth\"}'"}}]}}

{"type": "assistant", "timestamp": "2026-10-23T13:37:35.178Z", "parent_tool_use_id": null, "uuid": "e73192b8-885e-4b90-bbb9-ee826d84c4cf", "session_id": "90f1364c-d20b-4809-9a50-8356132da019", "message": {"model": "claude-sonnet-5-5", "id": "msg_011CgKG1oDX6Xb9UAxjWseE1", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_01XekHe7Z2m2rTkDn1GXqm9g", "name": "Bash", "input": {"command": "cd /app/.spektacular/work/20260101000000-user-auth\ncat > implementation_detail.md <<'EOF'\nThe feature introduces a new module boundary: an `auth` package that exposes small interfaces (token service, refresh store, deny list, audit emitter) and hides JWT, SQL and Redis specifics behind them. Handlers and middleware depend only on those interfaces, so each can be tested with in-memory fakes and the Redis or PostgreSQL implementations swapped without touching callers.\n\nRequest validation becomes a single middleware pipeline: extract bearer token \u2192 verify signature and expiry \u2192 check deny list \u2192 attach identity \u2192 emit audit record on rejection. All failure branches collapse into one error path that yields an identical 401 response, which removes the risk of leaking why a token failed. The audit emitter is invoked at the same decision points as the response, so audit coverage mirrors behaviour by construction.\n\nRefresh handling follows a rotate-on-use pattern: the presented token is hashed, looked up, atomically marked used and replaced with a fresh one in a single transaction. This pattern is new to the codebase; there is no existing code to follow, so conventional layering (handler \u2192 service \u2192 store) is introduced. Migration introduces a feature switch in route wiring: protected routes accept either legacy sessions or JWTs until cutover, after which the legacy branch is deleted. For a developer reading the code, authentication appears as one explicit middleware on route groups rather than ad-hoc checks per handler.\nEOF\ncat >> assumptions.md <<'EOF'\n\n### Handler-service-store layering (implementation_detail)\n- **Decision**: Introduce conventional layering with interfaces and fakes for tests.\n- **Rationale**: No existing patterns to follow; supports latency and testability goals.\n- **Rejected**: Handlers calling Redis/SQL directly (hard to test, couples transport to storage).\nEOF\ncd /app; spektacular plan goto --data '{\"step\":\"dependencies\",\"name\":\"20260101000000-user-auth\"}'"}}]}}

{"type": "assistant", "timestamp": "2026-10-23T13:37:58.009Z", "parent_tool_use_id": null, "uuid": "29146856-249c-49f7-9d0d-dd4977cd24a7", "session_id": "90f1364c-d20b-4809-9a50-8356132da019", "message": {"model": "claude-sonnet-5-5", "id": "msg_011CgKG3TXQ4nPstxprx3rdZ", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_01CeL9LkEa9Eiw8nEsrRmCNy", "name": "Bash", "input": {"command": "cd /app/.spektacular/work/20260101000000-user-auth\ncat > milestones.md <<'EOF'\n### Milestone 1: Users can log in and receive signed tokens\n**What changes**: A user with valid credentials can call the login endpoint and receive an RS256-signed 15-minute access token plus a 7-day refresh token. The refresh token is stored hashed in PostgreSQL, and every login outcome is audit-logged. Nothing about existing session-based endpoints changes yet.\n**Validation point**: Login integration test returns both tokens; decoded claims contain only user ID and role; database holds no raw refresh token; audit records are emitted.\n\n### Milestone 2: Protected routes accept and reject tokens correctly\n**What changes**: Authenticated requests are validated by middleware on every protected route. Valid tokens identify the user; expired, tampered or malformed tokens get an identical 401. Tokens issued by one instance work on any other, with no shared session state.\n**Validation point**: Middleware tests pass, the two-instance cross-validation test passes, and the p99 validation benchmark is under 5ms.\n\n### Milestone 3: Users can stay signed in and sign out securely\n**What changes**: Users exchange a refresh token for a new access token without re-entering credentials, and tokens can be revoked so they are rejected on the very next request. Revoked entries age out of Redis automatically.\n**Validation point**: Refresh and revoke integration tests pass, including rotation and deny-list TTL expiry.\n\n### Milestone 4: Existing services migrate with zero downtime\n**What changes**: Services cut over from sessions to JWT through a switch that lets both modes run side by side, so end users see no interruption and existing endpoints keep working. Legacy session handling is retired after cutover.\n**Validation point**: The full existing integration suite passes in both modes; staged cutover is observed with no downtime; load test sustains 1000 logins per second.\nEOF\ncat >> assumptions.md <<'EOF'\n\n### Four milestones ordered issue \u2192 validate \u2192 refresh/revoke \u2192 migrate (milestones)\n- **Decision**: Split into four independently deliverable milestones in that order.\n- **Rationale**: Each builds on the previous and yields user-visible behaviour.\n- **Rejected**: Single big milestone (poor reviewability); endpoint-per-milestone (no standalone value for revoke without validation).\nEOF\ncd /app; spektacular plan goto --data '{\"step\":\"tasks\",\"name\":\"20260101000000-user-auth\"}'"}}]}}

It signs RS256 access tokens that expire after 15 minutes with only user ID, role and a token ID as claims, and verifies signature and expiry using keys loaded from environment config.\",\n [\"Access tokens are RS256-signed, expire after 15 minutes and contain only user ID, role and token ID\",\"Tokens with a bad signature, a different algorithm or an expired timestamp fail verification\",\"Verification works with only the public key present\"],\n \"`auth/token_service:1` (new) \u2014 Issue/Verify; `auth/keys:1` (new) \u2014 load PEM keys from env; `auth/token_service_test:1` (new).\",\"Medium\",\"~25k\",\"2-3 parallel agents: key loading, signing/verifying, tests; integrate sequentially.\"),\n(\"ab75fa73-315b-4359-bf39-18d04ac7e5cd\",\"Add refresh token table and store\",[],\"agent\",\n \"Add the `refresh_tokens` PostgreSQL migration and a store that saves refresh tokens only as hashes. Failures return a uniform error and are audit-logged.\",\n [\"A user with valid credentials receives both tokens in a single response\",\"Invalid credentials are rejected and audit-logged without leaking which part was wrong\"],\n \"`auth/handlers/login:1` (new); `routes:1` \u2014 register `/auth/login`; `auth/handlers/login_test:1` (new).\",\"Medium\",\"~25k\",\"2-3 parallel agents: handler, route wiring, integration tests.\"),\n(\"cd7cc434-7146-4282-96c7-fbaa3493d53f\",\"Build auth middleware and Redis deny list\",[\"fa41ea9b-e54f-43be-9a86-b77a8caec004 \u2014 Build token service and key provider\",\"599e9010-a150-4a18-852b-afd2eef14d28 \u2014 Add AUTH_AUDIT_V2 audit emitter\"],\"agent\",\n \"Add the Redis-backed deny list and the middleware that validates the bearer token on protected routes. It attaches the verified identity to the request context and returns an identical 401 for expired, tampered, malformed or denied tokens.\",\n [\"Expired and invalid tokens return the same HTTP 401 without revealing the reason\",\"Denied tokens are rejected and deny entries expire when the token would have\",\"A token issued by one instance is accepted by another without shared session state\",\"Token validation stays under 5ms p99 in the benchmark\"],\n \"`auth/denylist:1` (new) \u2014 Redis SET with TTL; `auth/middleware:1` (new); `auth/middleware_test:1` (new); `auth/bench_test:1` (new) \u2014 p99 latency.\",\"High\",\"~50k\",\"Parallel analysis of deny list and middleware; sequential integration with benchmark.\"),\n(\"d6a1b187-a7d2-40f7-a194-d44237078d8a\",\"Implement refresh and revoke endpoints\",[\"ab75fa73-315b-4359-bf39-18d04ac7e5cd \u2014 Add refresh token table and store\",\"c1380d43-86d9-42f0-abea-3d51a5a4fd61 \u2014 Implement login endpoint\",\"cd7cc434-7146-4282-96c7-fbaa3493d53f \u2014 Build auth middleware and Redis deny list\"],\"agent\",\n \"Add `/auth/refresh`, which swaps a valid refresh token for a new access token and a rotated refresh token, and `/auth/revoke`, which denies the access token and invalidates the refresh token. They also provision the Redis instance the deny list uses in each environment.\",\n [\"Every environment has the key pair configured as the token service expects\",\"A Redis instance is reachable from every service instance\"],\n \"Person generates keys, loads secrets into each environment's config, provisions Redis, and confirms by running the cross-instance validation test.\",\"Low\",\"n/a\",\"Not applicable; human task.\"),\n]\np=open(\"tasks_plan.md\",\"w\"); c=open(\"tasks_context.md\",\"w\")\nfor id,t,deps,ex,s,ac,fc,cx,tok,st in tasks:\n    slug=t.lower().replace(\" \",\"-\")\n    d=\"\\n\".join(\"- \"+x for x in deps) if deps else \" none\"\n    dl=\"**Depends on:**\"+(\"\\n\"+d if deps else \" none\")\n    p.write(f\"#### - [ ] Task: {t}\\n**Id:** {id}\\n**Repo:** app\\n{dl}\\n**Execution:** {ex}\\n\\n{s}\\n\\n*Technical detail:* [context.md#task-{slug}](./context.md#task-{slug})\\n\\n**Acceptance criteria**:\\n\"+\"\\n\".join(\"- [ ] \"+a for a in ac)+\"\\n\\n\")\n    c.write(f\"### Task: {t}\\n\\n- **File changes**: {fc}\\n- **Complexity**: {cx}\\n- **Token estimate**: {tok} tokens\\n- **Agent strategy**: {st}\\n\\n\")\nEOF\ncat >> assumptions.md <<'EOF'\n\n### Task breakdown and proposed file paths (tasks)\n- **Decision**: Eight tasks in one repo (`app`); file paths are proposed new locations since the repo has no code; one human task for key and Redis provisioning.\n- **Rationale**: Greenfield repo, so paths are conventions to be confirmed; secrets/infrastructure require a person.\n- **Rejected**: Making reviews tasks (forbidden); one task per endpoint with no shared foundation tasks (duplicated work).\nEOF\nhead -30 tasks_plan.md; cd /app; spektacular plan goto --data '{\"step\":\"open_questions\",\"name\":\"20260101000000-user-auth\"}'"}}]}}

This lets backend services scale horizontally and gives end users reliable login across services.\n\n## Conventions\n\n{r('conventions.md')}\n## Architecture & Design Decisions\n\n{r('architecture.md')}\n## Component Breakdown\n\n{r('components.md')}\n## Data Structures & Interfaces\n\n{r('data_structures.md')}\n## Implementation Detail\n\n{r('implementation_detail.md')}\n## Dependencies\n\n{r('dependencies.md')}\n## Testing Approach\n\n{r('testing_approach.md')}\n## Milestones & Tasks\n\n{r('milestones.md')}\n{r('tasks_plan.md')}\n## Open Questions\n\n{r('open_questions.md')}\n## Out of Scope\n\n{r('out_of_scope.md')}\"\"\"\nctx=f\"\"\"# Context: {N}\n\n## Current State Analysis\n\nThe `app` repository root (/app) currently contains no source code, tests, configuration or migrations; only Spektacular guidance (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`). Legacy removal is out of scope.\n\n## Performance Considerations\n\nToken validation must add under 5ms p99: verify locally with the cached public key (no network call for signature checks) and do a single Redis lookup for the deny list.
